chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Playing the Kansas City Six sides; Freddie Green sings "Them There Eyes"
summary: Hinton plays Commodore sides with Lester Young and the Kansas City Six, and Jones says Freddie Green sang "Them There Eyes" in 1937.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Say, Jo, while we're playing records here, I'd like to play this wonderful one we've got here, a Commodore Jazz Classic Volume 4, called 'Prez'; Lester Young and the Kansas City Six, which of course includes you, Jo Jones, Lester Young, tenor and clarinet, Buck Clayton, trumpet, Freddie Green, guitar, Eddie Durham, electric guitar and trombone, and Walter Page on bass. You guys played "I Want a Little Girl", "Countless Blues", "Paging the Devil", and also "Four O'Clock Drag" and "Jo-Jo". So I think we should hear this because it's so beautiful and it shows some

of the very great work of some of the great Basie men like you and Buck Clayton, and here's Lester Young on tenor and clarinet, showing what a great clarinet player he was which people have forgotten sometimes I think. We also will hear some of the great work of Joe, (Walter Page), of Walter Page, and Eddie Durham - a great, great name in jazz, whose electric guitar and trombone are still around with us in 1973. I'd like to play this. The other side of this has got "Three Little Words", "Four O'Clock Drag", and "Jo-Jo", "Them There Eyes", and "Good Morning Blues", all in the order in which I just called them. On this last starting with "Three Little Words" we've got Lester Young on tenor; we've got Bill Coleman now on trumpet instead of Buck Clayton; we got Dickie Wells on trombone; we got Joe Bushkin on piano, the little king. We got John Simmons on bass, great bassist, and of course, Jo, you are here playing drums. So I think while we're having our little taste before lunch, or rather dinner, I wish we'd just listen to some more jazz. O.K.?
Say Jo, who was that sang that chorus on "Them There Eyes"? Sounded like Bill Coleman to me?
Yes, on that particular record that you just heard, a lot of people didn't know that Freddie Green was quite a vocalist and probably you will get them on the last

shot, that we did in 1937. We had some little cute tunes that they used to bring up. When you did the little cute tunes you would call them novelties but it was just an aside. On that particular record, "Them There Eyes", when we were making the Kansas City Five and the Six, that was Freddie Green's singing, "Them There Eyes".
